title: Residue-fibre complete-intersection charts cover after field extension
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$ be an affine open. Let $(U_b=\operatorname{Spec}B_b)_{b\in J}$ be affine opens of $X$, each mapping into $V$, with $f^{-1}(V)=\bigcup_{b\in J}U_b$. Fix a prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$, put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, and suppose each fibre algebra $S_b=B_b\otimes_Ak$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a finite type local complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra, def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Let $k\to K$ be any extension of fields, let $t:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$ be the composite through $\operatorname{Spec}k\to V$, and write $X_K=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}K$, $\pi:X_K\to X$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then the opens $W_b=\pi^{-1}(U_b)$ cover $X_K$. For each $b$ there are isomorphisms
$$W_b\cong\operatorname{Spec}(B_b\otimes_AK)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(S_b\otimes_kK)$$
of $K$-schemes. Under the first identification, the maps to $U_b$ and $\operatorname{Spec}K$ are the spectrum maps of $c\mapsto c\otimes1$ and $u\mapsto1\otimes u$. The second identification is induced by the $K$-algebra isomorphism $(c\otimes a)\otimes u\mapsto c\otimes au$, with inverse $c\otimes u\mapsto(c\otimes1)\otimes u$. Each $B_b\otimes_AK$ is a finite type local complete intersection over $K$. In particular $X_K$ is locally of finite type over $K$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and has an affine open cover by spectra of local-complete-intersection $K$-algebras. No condition is imposed on fibres at other primes, and $f$ need not be flat or locally of finite presentation; neither algebraicity nor algebraic closedness of $K$ is required. Empty fibres, zero algebras and empty covering families are allowed.

source.place: Tag 00SJ (lemma-lci-field-change), descent/ascent; schemes.tex Tags 01JR (lemma-open-fibre-product) and 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes); morphisms.tex Tag 01UG (lemma-local-complete-intersection). Explicit affine-chart and balanced-tensor comparison extracted from the proof of lem-trf-syntomic-geometric-fibres-affine-criterion, original steps 1, 3 and 6.

proof.text: Write $q:X_K\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ for the second projection. The fibre-product equation gives $f\circ\pi=t\circ q$. Since $t$ factors through $V$, every point of $X_K$ maps by $\pi$ into $f^{-1}(V)$. The assumed equality $f^{-1}(V)=\bigcup_b U_b$ therefore gives $X_K=\bigcup_b\pi^{-1}(U_b)$. Each $W_b=\pi^{-1}(U_b)$ is open by continuity of the scheme morphism $\pi$.

source.place: Tag 01JR (lemma-open-fibre-product): inverse-image opens and the projection equation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] to the two maps $X\to Y$ and $\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$, using the opens $V\subseteq Y$, $U_b\subseteq X$ and all of $\operatorname{Spec}K$. Its image formula identifies $U_b\times_V\operatorname{Spec}K$ with $W_b$, compatibly with both projections. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] with $R=A$, its first algebra $B_b$ and its second algebra $K$. This gives $W_b\cong\operatorname{Spec}(B_b\otimes_A K)$, and identifies its projections with the spectrum maps of $c\mapsto c\otimes1$ and $u\mapsto1\otimes u$. In particular this is an isomorphism over $\operatorname{Spec}K$.

Put $B=B_b$ and $S=B\otimes_A k$. Define $\Phi:S\otimes_k K\to B\otimes_A K$ on pure tensors by $\Phi((c\otimes a)\otimes u)=c\otimes au$. The inner $A$-balancing relation is respected because $rc\otimes au=c\otimes r a u$ for $r\in A$; the outer $k$-balancing relation is respected because $c\otimes(aa_0)u=c\otimes a(a_0u)$. Define $\Psi:B\otimes_A K\to S\otimes_k K$ by $\Psi(c\otimes u)=(c\otimes1)\otimes u$. For $r\in A$, $(rc\otimes1)\otimes u=(c\otimes\bar r)\otimes u=(c\otimes1)\otimes\bar r u$, so this too respects balancing. Both formulas are additive, preserve products and the unit, and send the $K$-scalar $u$ to $1\otimes u$. Their composites fix pure tensors: $\Phi\Psi(c\otimes u)=c\otimes u$, and $\Psi\Phi((c\otimes a)\otimes u)=(c\otimes1)\otimes au=(c\otimes a)\otimes u$. Thus they are inverse $K$-algebra isomorphisms. Taking spectra yields the claimed second isomorphism, over $K$.

source.place: Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes), tensor-product universal property; explicit balancing calculation for the iterated scalar extension.

proof.text: For each $b$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-lci-field-change] to the finite type $k$-algebra $S_b$ and the given field extension $k\to K$. It gives that $S_b\otimes_k K$ is finite type and a local complete intersection over $K$. The $K$-algebra isomorphism $\Phi$ of step 3 transfers these properties to $B_b\otimes_A K$: finite algebra generators map to finite algebra generators, and the principal-open cover and polynomial quotient presentations in [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field] map to the corresponding cover and presentations of the isomorphic algebra (the isomorphism and its inverse identify prime ideals and their strict-inclusion chains, hence preserve Krull dimensions).

source.place: Tag 00SJ (lemma-lci-field-change), ascent direction; Tag 00S9 (definition-lci-field), invariance of the defining presentations under algebra isomorphism.

proof.text: The opens in steps 1 and 2 are therefore an affine cover by spectra of finite type local-complete-intersection $K$-algebras. This is locally of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]: the only affine opens of the one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}K$ are itself and the empty open; their inverse images have respectively the displayed affine cover and the empty cover. No part of the construction uses any other fibre or any flatness, presentation or algebraic-closedness assumption. For a zero $S_b$, both tensor rings are zero and the corresponding chart is empty; the complete-intersection assertion is the zero-ring convention of [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. If the covering family is empty, step 1 forces $X_K$ empty, and every conclusion is vacuous or the same empty-cover assertion.
